svg.title: Chunking choices: splitter family, chunk size, and overlap
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure in two columns. The left column ranks three splitter families in order of preference: structure-aware, splitting on Markdown headings, HTML sections, code symbols, and page boundaries, best whenever the source has structure; sentence-aware, under a token budget, the default for free-form prose; and fixed-length, every N characters, a last resort that will cut sentences in half. A note adds that code splits by symbol. The right column shows chunk size as three zones on one bar: one to two hundred tokens is precise but not self-contained, four to six hundred is the sweet spot for prose, and a thousand or more wraps a fact in paragraphs you pay for. Below it, two bars drawn genuinely overlapping show the ten to twenty per cent of shared tokens that lets a fact on a boundary survive in at least one chunk in full. Captions cover parent-child and late chunking, and state that chunk size and splitter choice dominate retrieval quality while the vector database barely moves it.
svg.text: Chunking is more than half the battle
A chunk is the unit retrieval returns. Get it wrong and no amount of clever retrieval recovers.
Splitter, in order of preference
1 · Structure-aware
Markdown headings, HTML sections, code symbols, page bounds
Best whenever the source has structure to split on.
2 · Sentence-aware
Sentence boundaries, under a token budget per chunk
The default for free-form prose.
3 · Fixed-length
Every N characters or tokens, structure ignored
Last resort. It will cut sentences in half.
For code, split by symbol: a 1 200-token function is one chunk,
and so is a 50-token helper. Splitting mid-function is a mistake.
Size
precise, but
not self-contained
the sweet spot
for prose
wraps a fact in
paragraphs you pay for
Overlap
10–20% shared
A fact sitting on a boundary survives in at least one chunk
in full. The index grows linearly, which is cheap.
Decouple retrieved from embedded
Parent-child: embed small children for precision,
hand the model the larger parent for context.
Late chunking embeds the whole document first, then splits the token embeddings, so each vector already reflects its neighbours.
Both trade index complexity for recall on boundary-spanning facts. Reach for either once fixed chunking has plateaued.
Chunk size and splitter choice dominate retrieval quality. The vector database barely moves it.
